observations.surface: exported identifiers of packages itertools, core and free
observations.predicate: Input InterleaveShortest(slice(1,2,3),slice(-1,-2)); expected [1,-1,2,-2,3] because the longer input contributes one trailing element once the shorter is selected, whereas a stop-at-shorter implementation yields [1,-1,2,-2]

observations.surface: itertools.Fold, CollectVec, Sum1 and Product1 bulk specializations
observations.predicate: Rust's `size_hint() -> (usize, Option<usize>)` maps to `core.SizeHint{Lower,Upper}` with negative Upper meaning None: input `core.Hint(3,3)`; expected IsExact() true and {3,3}, while `core.RepeatIter(1).SizeHint()` equals {MaxInt,-1} with Bounded() false, which a plain tuple port cannot express

observations.surface: the panic behavior of itertools.ZipEq and itertools.Chunks
observations.predicate: Rust `panic!` becomes Go `panic`: input collecting ZipEq(slice(1,2,3),slice(1,2)); expected a recovered non-nil panic, and input constructing Chunks(slice(1,2,3),0); expected a recovered non-nil panic, whereas a migration that returns errors instead fails

observations.surface: core.ArrayWindows and core.CircularArrayWindows
observations.predicate: Input CircularArrayWindows(slice(1,2,3,4),3); expected [[1,2,3],[2,3,4],[3,4,1],[4,1,2]]; input CircularArrayWindows(slice(1,2),3); expected [[1,2,1],[2,1,2]], showing wrap-around that a non-wrapping window port cannot produce

observations.surface: itertools.ArrayWindows zero and short window boundary
observations.predicate: Input ArrayWindows(slice(1,2,3),0); expected exactly k+1 = 4 empty windows; input ArrayWindows(slice(1,2),3); expected no windows, whereas a naive implementation returning no windows for N==0 fails

observations.surface: core.Iter[T] protocol and each adaptor's Next/SizeHint plus NextBack capability
observations.predicate: Rust's `next() -> Option<T>` cannot be copied through: input `core.FromSlice([]int{7})`; expected the iteration protocol `Next() (int,bool)` returns (7,true) then (0,false) while `SizeHint()` returns {1,1} then {0,0}

observations.surface: runtime entry
observations.predicate: Rust macros become variadic Go functions: input Izip(slice(1,2,3),slice(10,20)); expected [[1,10],[2,20]]; input Iproduct(slice(1,2),slice(10,20)); expected [[1,10],[1,20],[2,10],[2,20]]; input ChainConcatenates(slice(1),slice(2,3),slice(4)); expected [1,2,3,4]

observations.surface: runtime entry
observations.predicate: Input `core.NewFormat(core.FromSlice([]int{1,2,3}),"-",nil).String()`; expected '1-2-3'; input a second String() call on the same value; expected a panic, reproducing Rust's consuming Display once-only contract

observations.surface: itertools.ExactlyOne and core.ExactlyOneError
observations.predicate: Input an empty iterator to AllEqualValue; expected a Go error with Error() exactly 'got zero elements when all elements were expected to be equal', and input slice(1,2) expected 'got different elements when all elements were expected to be equal'; a migration returning bare error values fails

observations.surface: runtime entry
observations.predicate: Input it.ExactlyOne(slice(2,3,4)); expected an error whose Error() is 'got at least 2 elements when exactly one was expected' and whose Next iteration restores 2,3,4, so consumed elements are not lost as they would be with a plain error return
